caption:
In all 18 maxillary specimens studied, the posterior superior alveolar artery and the infraorbital artery were connected by an anastomosis inside the lateral sinus wall. In 8 of 18 (44%), a second anastomosis ran outside the bone on the vestibular side. The intraosseous anastomosis lay on average about 19 mm above the alveolar ridge. These vessels are a reason to check the lateral wall on CBCT before a lateral window sinus floor elevation. Note: cadaver study of 18 specimens.

Source: Solar P, Geyerhofer U, Traxler H, Windisch A, Ulm C, Watzek G. Blood supply to the maxillary sinus relevant to sinus floor elevation procedures. Clin Oral Implants Res. 1999;10(1):34-44. PMID 10196788
